sections.overview: The Persian skipper occurs from the Balkans across Asia Minor toward Iran and the Caucasus.
sections.identification: The Albanian account gives males a forewing length of 14–15 mm and describes the species as larger than Spialia orbifer.
sections.habitat: It occurs on open, hot, dry grassland and rocky slopes, from low elevations to mountain sites.
sections.diet: The larval host is not firmly established across its range; caterpillars are reported on bindweeds, Convolvulus species.
sections.behavior: Adults visit low flowers for nectar, and regional accounts describe them as active in hot, open sites.
sections.reproduction: A Bulgarian regional account reports one flight generation in June and July; timing may differ elsewhere.
sections.ecology: Populations can be very local; recent surveys in Albania found new sites in the southeast but did not reconfirm some northern records.
sections.conservation: The European IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern in Europe and the EU, but this regional category does not establish its status across the full range.
